chunks: Yet they did not differ about it until knowledge came to them, through rivalries among themselves. If the Word of your Lord, (staying) it for a time ordained, had not preceded it, the matter would have been settled among them. But those who came to inherit the Book after them are also in doubt and disturbed about it.
ai.seo_question: Why did the Children of Israel divide after receiving knowledge?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the Ahl al-Bayt, suggesting that the 'knowledge' (al-'ilm) which preceded the division refers to the prophetic knowledge of the Imams, and the 'arrogance' (baghyan) reflects the Umayyad and Abbasid rivalries that fractured the community. The 'word' (kalimah) of respite is interpreted as the divine decree delaying the final judgment to allow for the emergence of the Mahdi, while the 'doubt' of later inheritors highlights the ambiguity in their claim to the true legacy of the Prophet. This context underscores the Shia view that unity was lost not due to lack of knowledge, but due to political ambition and deviation from the designated leadership.
